clarifications.title: RFC to Device Reference context
clarifications.authority: An RFC may hold Device Reference context directly, including when no Service Request is linked and when a subordinate RFC has device context distinct from its master/root RFC. The operational relationship is to a Device Reference. A Device Reference may remain unregistered or resolve to an Infrastructure Network Element without replacing the RFC relationship identity.
preserved_constraints: Service Request direct RFC linkage targets the master/root RFC while subordinate provenance is preserved.
Network Element identity does not replace Device Reference identity in operational ticket relationships.

clarifications.title: Infrastructure physical model
clarifications.authority: The physical Infrastructure model is Site -> Room -> Rack. Rack placement may carry row, column, and position semantics. Reusable Model/BOM/component compatibility knowledge is distinct from per-Network-Element installed Component identity and history. Installed Component history belongs to the physical Network Element instance and must not be collapsed into reusable model compatibility data.
preserved_constraints: Every regularized Network Element is anchored to one Site.
Rack placement cannot imply a different Site from the Network Element's authoritative Site.
Reusable compatibility data and installed-instance history remain separate authorities.

clarifications.title: SLA cohort identity correction
clarifications.authority: Compliance outcome is derived after cohort membership and is not part of cohort identity. The corrected current-HEAD Product Line/SLA rule governs implementation; the conflicting B002 assertion remains historical assurance evidence only.
